scenarios.name: Hero Section Display and Content
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays clear, compelling headline, tagline, and call-to-action buttons that communicate MirDB's core value proposition

steps.description: Load the product homepage in a browser
steps.context: Homepage should be accessible and render without errors

steps.description: Check for presence of logo, project name, tagline, description, and CTA buttons
steps.context: Hero section is the first visible area above the fold

steps.description: Verify tagline mentions 'Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' and highlights Rust performance and durability
steps.context: Content must align with REQ-1 requirements

test_cases.input: Load homepage and inspect hero section
test_cases.expected: Project logo is visible and properly sized
Headline clearly communicates MirDB's core value proposition as persistent memcached-compatible storage
Tagline reads 'Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' or similar
Get Started button is visible and clickable
View on GitHub button is visible and links to repository

scenarios.name: Key Differentiators and Features Section
scenarios.description: Verify the features section displays all key differentiators including Rust performance, persistence via SSTables, and memcached protocol compatibility

steps.description: Navigate to the features/differentiators section of the homepage
steps.context: Features section should be clearly visible and organized

steps.description: Check that all required features are displayed with appropriate icons/visuals
steps.context: Must include REQ-2 and REQ-4 requirements

test_cases.input: Check for Memcached Protocol Compatible feature
test_cases.expected: Feature card/item displays memcached protocol compatibility with description
Feature displays persistence via SSTables information
Feature displays LSM-tree storage architecture information
Feature highlights Rust performance benefits
Feature displays Write-Ahead Log for crash recovery/durability
Feature displays configurable compaction information

test_cases.input: Check for Skip List Memtable feature
test_cases.expected: Feature highlights skip list memtable implementation

scenarios.name: Supported Memcached Commands Display
scenarios.description: Verify the homepage displays supported memcached commands (SET, GET, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND)

steps.description: Find the section displaying supported memcached commands
Check that all seven required commands are displayed
steps.context: Commands should be clearly formatted and readable

test_cases.expected: SET command is listed in supported commands
GET command is listed in supported commands
DELETE command is listed in supported commands
ADD command is listed in supported commands
REPLACE command is listed in supported commands
APPEND command is listed in supported commands
PREPEND command is listed in supported commands

scenarios.name: Code Examples Section
scenarios.description: Verify code examples demonstrate basic operations with existing memcached clients, with syntax highlighting and copy functionality

steps.description: Locate the code example/usage demonstration section
steps.context: REQ-6 requirement - must have code examples

steps.description: Check that code blocks are syntax-highlighted and readable
Verify copy-to-clipboard button works correctly
steps.context: User experience feature for easy code copying

test_cases.expected: At least one code example showing memcached client usage is displayed
Code blocks have syntax highlighting applied
Click copy button copies code to clipboard successfully

test_cases.input: Verify code example demonstrates basic operations
test_cases.expected: Example shows SET and GET operations with a memcached client

steps.context: REQ-3 requirement - must have getting started guide

Check for basic commands to start using MirDB
steps.context: Should help user get started quickly

test_cases.expected: Clear installation instructions including cargo build command are present
Basic usage commands to run MirDB are displayed
Default configuration details (port 12333, etc.) are mentioned

scenarios.name: Architecture Diagram Section

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify the homepage is fully responsive and displays correctly on mobile viewports

steps.description: Resize browser or use device emulation for 375px width
Check all sections adapt properly to mobile layout
steps.context: Content should be readable and navigation accessible

steps.description: Verify buttons and links are touch-friendly
steps.context: Mobile users need adequate touch targets

test_cases.expected: All content is visible and readable without horizontal scrolling
Hero section adapts to mobile with readable text and accessible CTAs
Features stack vertically and are fully visible
Code blocks are scrollable horizontally or wrap appropriately
Buttons and links have minimum 44x44px touch target size

scenarios.name: Page Performance - Load Time
scenarios.description: Verify page loads within acceptable time limits (under 3 seconds on 3G)

steps.description: Use performance tools to measure load time
Execute Lighthouse performance audit

test_cases.expected: FCP is under 1.8 seconds
LCP is under 2.5 seconds
Lighthouse performance score is 90 or higher
Page is usable within 3 seconds on simulated 3G

scenarios.name: Accessibility - WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance
scenarios.description: Verify the homepage meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards

steps.description: Use Lighthouse or axe-core for accessibility testing
Perform manual keyboard and screen reader testing

test_cases.expected: Lighthouse accessibility score is 90 or higher
Page uses proper h1-h6 heading hierarchy without skipping levels
All images and diagrams have descriptive alt text
All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard (Tab, Enter)
All text meets WCAG AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large text)
Visible focus indicators are present on all interactive elements
Content is understandable when read by screen reader
